hilfe: Alloying: TWO different ores become ONE new material.
The result is worth more than its parts, shows up in your bag as its own
stack (own name, own colours, own pattern) and can then be processed
normally - polished, refined, and alloyed again if you like.
A result is NEVER minable. It is not in the ground, it only comes into
being here. That is why it is not in data/erze.json.
One line in "legierungen":
name      what the new material is called. That is how the player calls
it: item.alloy("Electrum") - and item.canAlloy("Electrum")
says beforehand how many pieces would work right now.
aus       the ingredients: ore and count per piece. At least two
DIFFERENT ores - otherwise it would not be alloying.
von       LIST of states the ingredients must be in. THIS is where you
set how much work comes first: with ["smelted"] you have to
smelt them, raw never works. Every ingredient must be in ONE
of these states - they may differ (the Electrum is already
alloyed, the silver next to it only smelted).
zu        state the result comes out in. Usually "alloy".
dauer     seconds per piece. Alloying uses the same single job slot as
processing - only ONE runs at a time.
reinheit  change in percentage points, may be negative. The purity of the
result is the count-weighted average of the ingredients plus
this value, clamped to 0..100.
wert      base value of the new material, like "wert" in data/erze.json.
The price works the same way: wert * zustandswert *
purity factor * money per block.
farbe1 / farbe2 / muster
how it looks in the bag. Pick something you can tell apart
from the ingredients.
zustaende which processing steps still work afterwards. The state from
"zu" always belongs in; if it is missing, it is added.
legierbar_mit
which ores the result can ITSELF be alloyed with - the same
field as in data/erze.json.
THE CHECK WITH "legierbar_mit":
A recipe only works if its ingredients list each other in
"legierbar_mit" in data/erze.json. If an entry is missing, the recipe
drops out and the message shows up in red in the game - so it is obvious
right away when the two files claim different things.
Please do not reorder this list: the results are appended to the ore list,
and the save file stores the NUMBER of an ore. Append new ones at the end.
